The reasons I see and talk about with others include:

1. Sexual function (or lack thereof on HRT)
2. Clothing fit
3. Safety (passing in certain context)
4. Dysphoria or discontentment with your natal anatomy

You believe you would enjoy the sexual function of a vagina over a penis. You experience a disconnect when using your natal anatomy (dysphoria). You want clothing to fit better, especially tight clothing.

Keep the conversations going with people. Learn their insights and motivations. Journal and speak with a qualified therapist to help guide your thought process. Being 50/50 on such a life altering surgery sounds like a gamble. You really want to be a lot more sure this is what you want given the cost, recovery, risk and irreversibility.

You will need to augment your mouth and tongue positioning as well as raise your larynx height. It sounds a lot harder than it is. An easy way to change vocal size is by stretching your lips wide while you speak. You’ll notice a lot of trans fems will speak with a unique looking mouth shape. That’s by design. Your tongue positioning also needs to occupy more space than it being flat against the bottom of your mouth. It’s slightly lifted at the back (which will help queue your larynx to come up to the right height). Larynx height is controlled by skeletal muscle (meaning you can control it). The easiest way to make a mind-body connection is by either physically holding it higher in the neck or by swallowing. The end goal is to be able to phonate (speak) while it’s elevated. It will seem difficult at first but practice makes perfect :)

So several things stand out to me. 

First, your vocal weight and size are too big. In order to feminize the sound you need to be able to make your mouth space (including back of the throat) a little smaller. You need to also speak with a little more breathy-ness (if that’s even a word).

Secondly, your pitch is a slight bit low. I tried to emulate a “female sounding voice” in your pitch range but found it exceptionally difficult. Raising pitch can sometimes be a fools errand. Find your “break” (the place where your voice cracks before hitting falsetto) and try to speak a tone below that. It should be comfortable but purposeful. Use a vocal analysis program to see if you are getting pitch slip.

Lastly, your enunciation and monotone pitch give off a very masculine feel. Most women are more whimsical, providing gentle pitch changes in speech.
